title: dual-passband-angular-stable-fss
description: PaperBench scoring tree for Li, Ma, Ren, Wang & Xiang, Micromachines 15(6), 690 (2024): A Dual-Passband Frequency Selective Surface with High Angular Stability and Polarization Insensitivity.

sub_tasks.title: Units, cell size and layer stack
sub_tasks.description: structure.json and the source code use consistent length units (mm or explicitly stated equivalent units). The unit cell is an 11.0 mm square (Table 1, P), with a single dielectric substrate of thickness 1.0 mm (SubH). Patterned metal covers only one substrate face: the upper, incident-side surface (Sec. 2.1 and the side view in Fig. 7). The pattern consists of apertures in metal, not metal patches. These facts must be consistent between structure.json and the source code, without contradictions.

sub_tasks.title: Concentric aperture geometry per Table 1 / Fig. 6
sub_tasks.description: The concentric aperture geometry matches Table 1/Fig. 6, from the unit-cell center outward: a central circular aperture of radius 1.5 (R4); a metal annulus spanning 1.5–3.0; an inner annular slot spanning 3.0–3.5 (inner radius R3=3.0, width W3=0.5); an intervening metal ring of width 1.0 (W2, spanning 3.5–4.5); an outer annular slot spanning 4.5–5.0 (inner radius R2=4.5, outer radius R1=5.0, width W1=0.5); and a metal border of width 0.5 between the outer slot and the cell edge (g/2 in Fig. 6). structure.json records these values consistently, satisfying R1=R2+W1 and R2=R3+W3+W2.

sub_tasks.title: Four cross apertures (X slots)
sub_tasks.description: The four cross-shaped slots match Fig. 2(c)/Fig. 6. Their centers lie on the unit-cell diagonals at distance R5=6.0 mm from the cell center (Cartesian coordinates ±4.243, ±4.243). Each cross consists of two perpendicular rectangular slots of length L1=2.0 and width W4=0.4, oriented at ±45° to the cell edges: X-shaped in an edge-aligned top view. Fig. 1 shows a + in a 3D view with the entire cell rotated 45°; Fig. 6 governs the orientation. The pattern has fourfold rotational symmetry. The inner endpoint of each radial arm reaches the outer edge of the outer annular slot (R5−L1/2=R1=5.0). These positions and dimensions can be reconstructed from structure.json.

sub_tasks.title: Materials
sub_tasks.description: The substrate is a duroid-type dielectric with relative permittivity 2.2, loss tangent 0.0009, and thickness 1.0 mm (Sec. 2.1). The metal is copper, with a thickness chosen within the paper's 0.017–0.035 mm range, or an equivalent finite-conductivity sheet approximation. Explain the choice and rationale in README/meta.json. Material settings are consistent across all 8 variants.

sub_tasks.title: Periodicity and unit-cell environment
sub_tasks.description: The lattice is square, with a period of 11.0 mm in both in-plane directions (Sec. 2.1, quadrilateral periodic pattern, and Table 1, P). The unit-cell sidewalls use periodic boundaries (lattice pairs, master/slave, or equivalent). Air regions above and below the cell terminate at ports. There are no additional layers beyond the single metal layer and substrate. The boundaries in structure.json record the periodic directions and unit-cell envelope.

sub_tasks.title: structure.json freeze quality
sub_tasks.description: structure.json satisfies the addendum schema, including model_units/parameters/materials/named_objects/boundaries/excitations/setups/ports. named_objects provides a textual reconstruction of all scored geometric facts: radii, widths, and positions of the five aperture classes, periodicity, substrate, and metal layer. All 12 parameters in Table 1 can be recovered.

sub_tasks.title: Unit-cell top-view structural visual audit
sub_tasks.description: submission/views/unit_cell/top.png, with cell edges aligned to the image axes, shows a central circular aperture, two concentric annular slots, the intervening metal ring, four corner X-shaped slots with arms at ±45°, and a continuous metal border. The topology matches Fig. 2(c)/Fig. 6, and aperture proportions visually agree with structure.json. Score 0 for any missing feature, extra structure, or incorrect cross orientation (+ rather than X).

sub_tasks.title: Unit-cell 3D/side structural visual audit
sub_tasks.description: submission/views/unit_cell/oblique_3d.png shows a single patterned metal layer on the upper surface of the dielectric substrate, no metal on the lower surface, and a substrate much thinner than the cell width (approximately 1 vs 11 mm). The stack matches Fig. 1/Fig. 7 and structure.json. Score 0 for reversed layer order, metal on both faces, or multiple dielectric layers.

sub_tasks.title: Evidence-based paper audit without a contradiction quota
sub_tasks.description: PAPER_AUDIT.md covers the three public review domains: geometry/materials, result claims, and formulas/conventions. At least two substantive checks include locatable paper evidence, the verification process, a conclusion, the resolution, and its impact. Findings may be contradictions, ambiguities, or verified consistency. No fixed number of contradictions or match to a private checklist is required; valid findings outside the checklist are equally acceptable. Disregard each incorrect or unsupported entry individually, without invalidating other qualifying checks. Explicitly reporting no contradictions can pass when supported by verification evidence. A generic claim of no issues, or copying the addendum without independent verification, is insufficient.

sub_tasks.title: Real PyAEDT/HFSS run chain
sub_tasks.description: The entry script under submission/src/ contains a real ansys.aedt.core Hfss analyze()/analyze_setup() call on the code path that produces the submitted results. The contract entrypoint is `submission/src/run_all.py`: `python3 src/run_all.py --variant <name>` runs the full HFSS workflow for that variant. If it is absent, use the entrypoint identified in README and note the missing contract entrypoint in the reason; the analyze criterion is unchanged. The call must not be bypassed through if False, a dry-run switch, a cache branch, or swallowed exceptions. The setup name matches setup_names in te_00 and te_86 meta.json files and the corresponding run.log entries.

sub_tasks.title: Unit-cell periodic + Floquet port configuration
sub_tasks.description: Use an HFSS driven solution, periodic unit-cell sidewalls (lattice pairs, master/slave, or equivalent), and Floquet ports above and below the cell. Each variant's scan angle and polarization match its name, such as θ=86° and TE for te_86, and are recorded in the four meta.json fields angle_convention/incident_plane/polarization_definition/floquet_phase_or_scan_settings. These agree with addendum Clarification 1: the incidence plane is x–z, φ=0°, and TE means E perpendicular to that plane. Periodic-boundary phases and port scan angles use the same (θ,φ).

sub_tasks.title: Sweep and export grid contract
sub_tasks.description: Each variant includes an adaptive solve and a frequency sweep covering 3–16.5 GHz. The exported sparams.csv uses the addendum's exact 0.01 GHz grid: 1351 rows from 3.00–16.50, with frequency_GHz,S11_dB,S21_dB columns. meta.json frequency_sweep agrees with the source sweep settings. Spot-check row counts, step size, and column names in the te_00 and tm_83 CSV files.

sub_tasks.title: Polarization/mode mapping of exported S-parameters
sub_tasks.description: S11/S21 are the power-normalized fundamental Floquet coefficients for the variant's actual polarization and angle; do not select traces blindly by mode index. Native modes include at least the two orthogonal fundamental modes, with mode settings supporting high-frequency convergence. Record mode orders, E/H polarization bases, native report expressions, and normalization in meta.fundamental_trace_map or a resolvable reference. excitation_summary/polarization_definition may reference that single mapping without duplicating it. Source code and native settings must agree. Assess the saved native modes, lattice basis, report expressions and normalization together. Existing native settings and resolvable source records may supply the mapping without duplicate prose or a separately exported polarization-vector file. A response-trend heuristic alone is insufficient; a verified correct native mapping is not invalidated solely by that heuristic.

sub_tasks.title: Native adaptive convergence evidence
sub_tasks.description: Verify the native convergence metric for every HFSS physical solve required by this task: Max Mag. Delta S <= 0.02 for port-driven solutions; HFSS native relative Delta Energy <= 0.02 is acceptable for finite plane-wave scattering. Logs/convergence tables include the actual final value, pass count, and native convergence status; every meta.mesh_summary has a positive tetrahedra count. Shared physical solutions may cover variants through solve_ids mappings in run_summary. Process Normal completion alone does not establish adaptive convergence. Pass only if all physical solutions qualify; identify each failed or unsupported solve_id. Honest disclosure is assessed separately in B1_5b.

sub_tasks.title: Convergence disclosure and fine-feature meshing
sub_tasks.description: README describes the static method, variant/dependency mapping, and the results/run_summary.json path. The current run report covers every variant, maps them to physical solutions through solve_ids, and records each solution's convergence metric, final value, pass count, mesh count, native-log location, and failure reason, consistently with actual evidence. Statistics for a shared physical solution may be recorded once. Dated historical statistics need not match a new run value for value; do not require replay to rewrite README. An unconverged solution can pass this item if honestly reported. Also check Floquet settings, mesh handling, pass limits, and convergence targets at extreme scan angles.

sub_tasks.title: Native AEDT/HFSS log authenticity
sub_tasks.description: Spot-check te_00, tm_30, te_86, and tm_83 using run.log together with original, replay-bound native AEDT/HFSS convergence, mesh-statistics and profile exports (for example .conv, .ms and .prof, or equivalent native exports). Each sampled physical solution must provide at least 3 distinct classes of native evidence across these records: (a) adaptive pass numbers and Max Mag. Delta S/ΔS values; (b) paired solve start/completion or native sweep completion; (c) convergence and mesh statistics, including tetrahedra/mesh elements counts; (d) native report/export records; (e) AEDT Message Manager severity records or native solver profiles, excluding PyAEDT wrapper INFO/WARNING lines alone; (f) native project-result or solver-profile paths linked to the actual solve. The corresponding meta.json setup_names must be identifiable in the original log or native headers. Verify the actual design, setup, variation and declared shared-solve relationship against saved native evidence and source. Native exports must be bound to the current replay and agree with MANIFEST hashes and sizes; byte identity alone does not prove authenticity or the correct physical solution. Native rows and hashes need not be copied into run.log, and absent transcription is not a failure here or under another item. A shared-solve variant may use its parent solution records when result_source and the actual variant mapping support that relationship. Python-generated assertions, timestamps, filenames, keyword lists or merely mentioning HFSS/Ansys do not qualify. Missing or invalid MANIFEST log indices belong to B2_5, not this scientific authenticity check.

sub_tasks.title: Cross-variant solve independence with declared-sharing exemption
sub_tasks.description: Using meta.result_source, run_summary, and native exports, verify an actual solve for each required geometry, angle, and orientation. An Optimetrics session may reuse a parent log, but physical solutions must be distinguished by solve_id, design, setup, variation, and excitation, with exports mapped individually. Identical log hashes, equal pass counts, or similar curves alone do not prove copying. Declaring sharing cannot replace a required independent physical solve. Fail only when evidence shows different physical variants actually reused one response, or when a required solve mapping is missing. Legitimate multi-polarization/multi-port processing of one solution follows the addendum.

sub_tasks.title: Paper-reading blacklist on result-feeding paths
sub_tasks.description: Blacklisted literals are paper output values: Table 2 insertion losses {0.36, 0.24, 0.98, 0.12, 0.23, 0.84, 0.59, 0.71, 0.08, 0.30, 0.10, 0.76, 0.52, 0.70, 0.99}; relative bandwidths {28.6, 27.3, 28.3, 27.4}, in percentage or decimal form; and measured insertion losses {3.59, 4.68, 1.07, 2.9, 2.88, 3.05}. Score 0 only when these literals occur as right-hand-side values on code paths writing data to submission/results/*.csv|*.json, including direct assignments, fallback branches, and hard-coded returns. Frequencies, angles, geometry dimensions, and material parameters are not blacklisted. Exemptions are defined in the addendum's Raw exports and offline derivation section and blacklist.md, including assertion/comparison constants, comments/debugging, and unrelated substrings.

sub_tasks.title: Provenance consistency
sub_tasks.description: Maintain a complete, consistent provenance chain linking project/design, setup, variation, excitation, UTC time, native logs, raw MANIFEST, and results. result_source/report_export_summary may use public structured references without copying MANIFEST contents. Each response and image must be traceable to its solution and export; merely mentioning HFSS is insufficient. Log-index formatting and completeness are assessed by B2_5, not charged again here. Inspect the existing native records to establish actual source identity; formatting leniency never permits an untraceable solution or excitation.

sub_tasks.title: Native export presence and manifest integrity
sub_tasks.description: Every HFSS variant has a nonempty raw/ directory and MANIFEST. Exports are preserved byte for byte, with file, sha256, bytes, producer, aedt_solution, run_log_lines, and exported_utc for each entry, and locatable design/variation/excitation. Check every manifest and sample native files, hashes, and log lines from at least two distinct physical solutions. Moving or renaming files without changing bytes is valid; reordered columns, converted units, or filtered rows are not raw exports. This item owns missing or invalid MANIFEST log indices. Native log lines need not contain SHA-256 digests; hashes are verified against the actual files. Export records may use the original export name.

sub_tasks.title: Independent native-to-output numerical consistency
sub_tasks.description: The trusted verifier independently verifies all eight replayed response arrays against their manifest-linked native exports and recomputes every required CSV-derived summary field and metric status. Required values must be finite, grids complete, and native/output/summary values consistent under the public direct/derived tolerances. Direct native dB values use absolute tolerance 1e-5 dB; derived summary values use 1e-3 dB and grid-selected frequencies use 1e-8 GHz. Optional candidate validation code, its filename, its coverage and its exit status are not scored. No candidate self-check script or receipt is required. Numerical agreement is decided by code, not a second LLM vote. Native physical source identity, image provenance and MANIFEST log indices remain covered by their existing audit leaves. A verifier reader limitation leaves this item unknown rather than creating a scientific failure.

sub_tasks.title: TE/TM coincidence at normal incidence (Fig. 9 target)
sub_tasks.description: Polarization-insensitivity target: coincident curves are the reproduction objective, so distinctness does not apply. The absolute S21 difference between te_00 and tm_00 sparams.csv is ≤ 0.25 dB at all six frequencies {5.00, 7.00, 8.45, 12.76, 14.00, 15.50} GHz. The differences between their summary band1_3dB lower edges and upper edges are each ≤ 0.06 GHz. A fourfold-symmetric cell has exact polarization degeneracy at normal incidence; both curves come from the same solution on the same mesh, so graph-reading and cross-version uncertainties do not affect their difference. The paper's own 0.07–0.08 GHz endpoint differences are reporting scatter, not grounds for a tolerance.

sub_tasks.description: **Independent of the paper; assess only the submission itself.** (a) All reflection/transmission coefficient magnitude columns satisfy passivity: each dB value is ≤ +0.04 dB and each linear magnitude is ≤ 1.005. (c) Phase columns use the contract's declared domain: wrapped to (−180°, 180°] or continuously unwrapped as specified.
